date: The Khaybar Expedition, 7th year of the Hijra (628)
title: 162nk1o
Khaybar and the Banner: "I Will Give It to One Who Loves God and His Messenger"
hook: Khaybar held out for days. The Prophet gave the banner to Imam Ali, whom God and His Messenger love.
scenes.0.text: In the seventh year of the Hijrah, the Prophet (peace be upon him) marched with his army to Khaybar, north of Medina. Khyber was a fortified settlement built in the midst of fruitful palm trees. Each was protected by high walls and heavy gates. The Muslim army surrounded the castles one by one. As the days passed, the heat of the desert and the fatigue of the siege fell upon the soldiers. Some castles fell, but the strongest ones held out. This siege would show everyone to whom the Prophet would entrust the most difficult task.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.1.text: One of the castles hasn't been taken in days. First Abu Bakr took the banner and marched to the fortress, but returned before completing the conquest. The next day, Umar took the flag. And he came back before he opened the castle door. There's been trouble in the camp. The soldiers were looking at the walls of the fortress, talking about how to break this resistance. **Ali**, on the other hand, was sleeping in his tent because of severe pain in his eyes and could not go to war. The Prophet watched everything quietly. He hadn't yet spoken his true word about who would carry the banner.
scenes.2.text: The Prophet gathered his companions in the evening and said, "I will give the flag of tomorrow to whoever loves Allah and His Messenger, and whoever loves Allah and His Messenger. Allah will grant victory by his hand". The prophet didn't say a name. That was the only word spoken in the tents that night. And the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) slept each one expecting to be given a banner. This is what Buhari and Muslim are saying. All through the night, everyone in the camp waited for the morning.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.text: And it came to pass in the morning, that all the people were gathered to the tent of the prophet. The Prophet looked at the crowd and asked, "Where is **Ali**?" They said, "His eyes hurt". She called him. When Ali was brought, the Prophet put his blessed spit on his eyes and his eyes were immediately healed. Then he handed the banner to Ali. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall I fight until they are Muslims like us?" And he said, Go, make no haste. First, call them to Islam and tell them the truth about Allah. By Allah, it is better for you that He guided a single soul through you than that you should have a red camel".
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.4.text: When **Ali** arrived at the front of the fort with the banner, the door opened and **Merhab**, the most famous warrior of Khyber, appeared. He was wearing a helmet and a breastplate. Waving his sword, he recited a poem and said that Khaybar recognized him, that his weapon was sharp. Ali walked up to him, and he replied poetically, "I am the one my mother named Haydar". Haydar means lion. According to Ahl-i Beyt's narratives, Ali lowered his sword on Zulfikar only once, and this blow brought Merhab to the ground. With the fall of Khyber's strongest warrior, the defenders were discouraged and the fortress was quickly captured.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.5.text: Another scene from that day is related in the Ahl-i-Bayt's narratives. At the height of the battle, **Ali** tore down the heavy gate of the Khyber fortress and fought with it in front of him like a shield. He met his arrows and blows through this door. His friends have been telling him about this power for years. Rumours do not give an exact measure of the weight of the gate, but they all attribute this power to Khyber's conquest. The Shia recall the Prophet's words in the evening when he narrated this scene: "Allah will grant victory by his hand".
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.text: The banner was given by the word of the Prophet to those who loved Allah and His Messenger and were loved by them. That person was **Ali**. The Prophet also described him as a man who did not shy away from battle and was always thrown forward. In the old days, there were those who returned without taking the castle. It wasn't a disgrace for anyone to go back to war. But it was in full view of everyone who the Prophet called out on the most difficult day of the army. This choice was based on the love of Allah and His Messenger. The companions of Sa'd b. Years later, when he was recounting the virtues of Ali, he would mention the flag of Khyber.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.text: After the fall of Khaybar, the inhabitants of the fortresses agreed to remain on their lands on the condition of giving half their produce. And the men of Fadak, who were nearby, made a treaty not to fight, not to draw the sword. This land, taken without a fight, belonged directly to the Prophet. The Prophet also donated the palms of Fedak to his daughter **Fatimah** and left them to her. A grant is a gratuitous gift. Fadak became a legitimate source of livelihood for the house of Fatima. However, after the Prophet's death, this garden would be taken from Fatimah's hand and Fadak would be the name of the expropriated right of the Ahl-i Beyt.
sunni.0.says: At Khaybar the banner is given to the one who loves God and His Messenger. Imam Ali's eyes are opened. Imam Ali says, "Shall I fight them until they become like us?" The Prophet tells him to go gently, to invite them to Islam, and states that guiding one person is better than red camels.
sunni.1.says: The flag is given to Ali. Ali asks, "Should I fight until they become Muslims like us?" And when thou comest into the house, call to Islam, and proclaim the truth. "God's guidance through you is better than the red camel". The text is No. It's in 3009; the store number is 4210.
sunni.2.says: The same banner dialogue. Imam Ali says, "O Messenger of God, shall I fight them until they become like us?" The Prophet tells him to proceed gently, invite them to Islam, and inform them of the rights of God. Guiding one person is better than owning red camels.
sunni.3.says: It is related that after the two earlier attempts, the banner was given to Imam Ali.
sunni.4.says: Marhab comes out into the field in armor saying "Khaybar knows that I am Marhab." Imam Ali replies, "I am the one whom my mother named Haydar," strikes him on the head and kills him. The conquest takes place through his hand. Splitting the helmet from the top in two, receiving no wound, and going to Hell are not in this text.
shia.0.says: The giving of the banner to Imam Ali at Khaybar, the narration of the gate, and the account of the event in Shia sources.
shia.1.says: The killing of Merhab by Ali in Khyber. The helmet and the head split in half in one blow didn't make a separate page. He left the stage as the Ehl-i-Beit legend.
shia.2.says: Merhab's curse, Ali's curse and the murder of Merhab.
disputes.0.title: 1smrgrr
What does the banner saying show?
disputes.0.shia: The Prophet said that he would give the banner of Khaybar to the one who loves Allah and His Messenger and is loved by them. The fact that the word is specific to him in Shi'a indicates his place and dignity with the Prophet; the failure of the previous two attempts shows this difference.
disputes.0.sunni: The Prophet said that he would give the banner of Khaybar to the one who loves Allah and His Messenger and is loved by them. This is a great virtue in Sunni reading, and there are similar praises for other companions, and the word is not a proof of caliphate.
disputes.1.title: 7duodm
The narration of Abu Bakr and Umar
disputes.1.shia: A tradition that the flag was first given to Abu Bakr, then to Umar. Hanbel is mentioned in the Musnad. The Shi'a cite this tradition as evidence of why it was special that the banner was given to Ali at the end.
disputes.1.sunni: A narration that the banner was given first to Abu Bakr and then to Umar is mentioned in al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak and Ahmad b. Hanbal, Musnad. In the Sunni reading, the authenticity of this narration is disputed; this detail is not in the narrations of Bukhari and Muslim.
disputes.2.title: 7tadab
The narration of the gate
disputes.2.shia: It is related that Imam Ali tore the gate of Khaybar from its place and used it. In Shia thought, this is an indication of his extraordinary strength.
disputes.2.sunni: It is related that Imam Ali tore the gate of Khaybar from its place and used it. Sunni hadith scholars regard the chain of this narration as weak; it is not found in the sahih sources.
questions.0: Abu Bekir and Umar had gone to the castle with the flag and returned without opening the door. Why do you think the Prophet left the flag until the next morning without naming who would take it in the evening, saying, "Love Allah and His Messenger"?
questions.1: Ali is in his tent because of the pain in his eyes, and he can't go to war. Why do you think the Prophet called Ali, who had pain in his eyes, to give him the banner?
questions.2: Ali said, "Should I fight until they are Muslims like us?" Why do you think the Prophet asked for an invitation to Islam before the battle?
summary: He said that the banner of the Prophet in Khaybar would be given to anyone who loves Allah and His Messenger and is loved by them. That person became Ali. This word also occurs in Sunni sources (Buhari, Sahih, no. 2942; Muslim, Sahih, no. 2406). The Shi'a consider this proof of Ali's place with the Prophet.
key: The banner was given to Imam Ali, who loves God and His Messenger
notes.0: Khaybar was a Jewish oasis north of Medina in the 7th year of the Hijra.
notes.1: One of the fortresses could not be taken for days.
notes.2: The Prophet said, «I will give the banner to one who loves God and His Messenger» (Bukhari 2942, Muslim 2406).
notes.3: The banner was given to Imam Ali; his eyes were healed by the Prophet's saliva.
notes.4: This saying is a sign of Imam Ali's being chosen.
sunni.5.says: Abu Rafi: Ali took a door next to the fortress and used it as a shield and held it until the conquest. Then eight people tried to open that door, but they couldn't.
sunni.5.grade: Sunni hadith scholars consider some of the longer forms of door narratives to be weak or obscene.
